page: Microsoft Azure E32-16ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the EDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores operating at 2.8 GHz. The processor architecture is x86_64 and includes 48 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware flags such as AVX-512 (AVX512F and AVX512_VNNI) for vector operations and VAES for accelerated cryptography. The instance is equipped with 256 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per vCPU. It also includes 1229 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark results place this instance in the average performance tier across multiple categories. In compute testing, the system achieved a single-core stress-ng score of 1898.98 and a multi-core score of 15534.57, while the PassMark CPU score reached 21361.52. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only cached small-block bandwidth of 834.58 GB/sec, which drops to 101.12 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads, and a write bandwidth of 58.35 GB/sec. Database operations on PassMark scored 8047.55, and Redis SET operations reached 15.94 million operations per second. For lightweight machine learning tasks, the instance processes 1082.45 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model, though performance drops to 35.05 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a resource density perspective, the E32-16ds_v5 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high GPU acceleration, as it lacks a dedicated GPU. The inclusion of 1229 GB of local SSD storage reduces the need for external block storage for temporary data, though users must manage the ephemeral nature of local disks. Given the high memory capacity and solid database benchmark performance, this instance is suited for relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, data analytics, and memory-heavy enterprise applications.
